extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying peer review; journal editors; publishers; research funders; scholarly communication professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A review-identifying core gaps and priorities in empirical and theoretical understanding of scholarly peer review, aimed at guiding research agendas, policy, and practice for editors, publishers, and funders. It summarizes themes, high-priority gaps, and recommended infrastructure and standards to advance peer review studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial responsibility is identified as a core theme in understanding peer review — the role editors play in decision-making and in upholding the integrity of the scholarly record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and clarify editors' duties, expectations, and influence on outcomes; consider how editorial actions distribute prestige and affect research evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and justification in editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-priority gap: the need for increased accountability and justification in decision-making processes for editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop practices and evidence requirements that make editors' decisions more transparent and justifiable (e.g., documented rationales, appeals, audit trails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity and bias of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The subjectivity and bias of reviewers is a core theme affecting the fairness and reliability of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study sources and manifestations of reviewer bias; design interventions or training to detect, mitigate, or account for subjective judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function and quality of peer review (quality assurance / quality control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the function and quality of peer review — its role as a method for establishing quality or scholarly legitimacy, and its effectiveness as quality assurance/control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically evaluate whether and how peer review ensures methodological rigor, correctness, clarity, and fitness for publication; identify metrics of review quality and processes that improve it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility as a dimension of peer review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility is named among keywords as a relevant concern related to peer review's ability to support reliable published findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how peer review processes assess and promote reproducibility (e.g., data/code review, replication checks) and how review workflows could better support reproducible research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and epistemic implications of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review has social and epistemic consequences, including how it distributes academic prestige and shapes knowledge production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study downstream social impacts, power dynamics, gatekeeping effects, and how review practices influence what counts as legitimate knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical understanding of the social impact of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-priority gap: developing a deeper, empirical understanding of the social impact of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct empirical research on how peer review affects careers, research agendas, diversity/inclusion, citation patterns, and broader scholarly communication ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (as a design/assessment dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is highlighted (keyword) as an alternative/modality relevant to assessing and redesigning peer review systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine openness (e.g., signed reports, published reviews, open identities) as a variable affecting accountability, quality, bias, and community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus minimal standards for what constitutes peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to design a consensus for a minimal set of standards for what constitutes peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop community-agreed definitions and minimal procedural/data elements (what activities, documentation, and checks must be present) to allow consistent study and benchmarking of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared data infrastructure for peer review research
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to develop a shared data infrastructure to support empirical study of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build interoperable, privacy-aware data repositories and standards (reviews, decisions, timelines, metadata) to enable reproducible research into peer review processes and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained funding and commitment from publishers and research funders
rubrics_metrics.description: The field requires sustained funding and commitment from publishers and research funders, who have responsibility to uphold the integrity of the published record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure long-term resources and institutional buy-in for infrastructure, studies, and implementation of reforms to peer review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing peer review studies as a research discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper advocates for the development of a new research discipline based on the study of peer review and presents a guide for the future of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate methodological standards, training, funding, and community-building to professionalize peer review studies and integrate findings into policy and practice.
